articles.title: WoW: Forever Aspires To Have A “Mandela Effect” On Players
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever is reinventing the classic version of Azeroth with all kinds of new content, and if Blizzard does its job, players won't be able to tell the difference between what's old and what's new.
body: Announced during BlizzCon 2026, Forever introduces four new zones to Azeroth: the Riverglades, Mount Hjyal, Shen'dralas, and Zephras Isle. In an interview with GameSpot, WoW: Forever senior art director Jeff Parrott and senior game designer Josh Greenfield elaborated on how Blizzard approached developing these all-new zones so that they don't feel out of place in a 22-year old game, as well as how they tried to capture how players "remember" Azeroth looking.
Parrott said the team spent a lot of time looking back at the original, "vanilla" version of WoW and trying to understand how zones were designed back in 2004 when the game first released.

"The team did a great job of just digging in there," Parrott said. "Riverglades is a great example. I think that's a full new zone that we have, and really did a great job of leaning into that Vanilla-era kind of ethos for the design, the flow in the way everything kind of moves through the zone, the quests move you through the zone. It does feel extremely of that era, of that time. So it's really just understanding what we're aiming for and staying faithful to it."
He said the goal was for Forever's new zones to feel "familiar, but new."

articles.title: New Darkwing Duck Series Announced for Disney+ Starring Mark Hamill and Seth Rogen
articles.summary: Disney+ has officially greenlit a new Darkwing Duck animated series with a voice cast led by Mark Hamill in the title role and Seth Rogen, who is also one of the new show’s producers. A teaser video was also released, which can be seen below.
body: “For the last 35 years, Darkwing Duck has been trapped in his worst nightmare: an alternate world that’s never heard of his superhero exploits. Now a rebellious teen named Duckie who knows all about his heroic past shows up to pull this ego-fueled vigilante back into battle,” according to the official plot synopsis.
“Together, this unlikely duo will get dangerous to fight old enemies like Negaduck and Megavolt and reunite with allies Launchpad, Gosalyn and Morgana to save the entire universe.”

In addition to Hamill as Drake Mallard aka Darkwing Duck and Rogen as Launchpad McQuack, the voice cast also includes Lizzy Caplan as Gosalyn Mallard, Lilimar as Duckie, Dan Stevens as Glade McTowers, Tiffany Shepis as Rosa, Kathryn Newton as Firecracker, Teo Briones as Timb, Tyler Dean Flores as Pondsy, Katie Rich as Officer Shanks, and Nat Faxon as Officer Webb.

Sean Tretta (Star Trek: Picard) and Borja Peña Gorostegui (Lost & Crowned), are executive producers. Seth Rogen, Evan Goldberg, James Weaver, Alex McAtee and Gabby Grantham are producing for Point Grey Pictures. Tad Stones, the creator of the original Darkwing Duck series, consulted on the development of this new series.

articles.title: Switch 2 Storage Deal: Get a 512GB Memory Card for $99.99
articles.summary: If you could use more storage on your Nintendo Switch 2 – and who among us couldn't? – here’s a deal for you. Amazon is offering a 512GB MicroSD Express card from Samsung for $99.99.
body: It's easy to miss if you don't follow such things, but the Nintendo Switch 2 is only compatible with microSD Express cards – not standard microSD cards like you probably used on your original Switch, or Steam Deck, or other handheld device. MicroSD Express cards have much faster read/write speeds, and the Switch 2 takes advantage of that, which means standard microSD cards won’t cut it in this high-tech age.

In the age of 4K graphics, video games take up more space now than ever before. And since the Switch 2 only comes with 256GB of onboard storage, and even many physical games require downloads, you’re likely to run out before long. For instance, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth takes up nearly 100GB of that space, and that's just one game!

That means you’ll probably want to add more storage sooner rather than later. But with prices of all kinds of computer components skyrocketing this year thanks to RAMageddon – and storage is absolutely included in that – it can cost a whole lot to add extra space for your games. Unless, that is, you can find a (relatively, for 2026 pricing) good deal on a microSD Express card. Like this one.

articles.title: What Is Xbox Game Studios At This Point?
articles.summary: The organizational structure of Xbox has long been complex and unwieldy, and that hasn't changed after the latest wave of changes and layoffs as part of Xbox's "reset." But Microsoft's latest reshuffling of its studios and workforce does prompt the question of what the "Xbox Game Studios" brand…
body: Not included is Mojang, the Minecraft studio that Microsoft has been leaning heavily on -- that studio now reports directly to Xbox CEO Asha Sharma.

Former studios under the Xbox Game Studios brand include Rare and World's Edge, the developer of Age of Empires, but both now fall under Activision Blizzard. And while it's unclear if Halo Studios as an organization is now formally an Activision Blizzard entity, it's official that Activision is indeed making the next Halo game. Meanwhile, Xbox studio Obsidian Entertainment has jumped to Bethesda, and Turn 10 has merged with Playground Games.

Technically, all of these development teams are still Xbox studios, and Xbox will continue to publish games from partners, like OD and Physint from Kojima Productions. But the state of "Xbox Game Studios" as its own publishing label is a curiosity.

It's not outside the realm of possibility that Microsoft is doing away with the branding altogether. Since mid-2025, the Xbox website has lacked any dedicated webpages or references to Xbox Game Studios. Contrast that with PlayStation Studios, which has its own page and lists 17 studios under Sony's umbrella.
points: The organizational structure of Xbox has long been complex and unwieldy, and that hasn't changed after the latest wave of changes and layoffs as part of Xbox's "reset.
But Microsoft's latest reshuffling of its studios and workforce does prompt the question of what the "Xbox Game Studios" brand…

articles.title: Wardogs Season 2 Release Date Announced, Will Add Weather Including Rain
articles.summary: Wardogs Season 2 has a release date, and the new content update will add weather effects, including rain. Wardogs Season 2 will arrive on October 15, and although we don't know much about it yet, we do know that it will add weather to the game.
body: Whether this will add any changes to the gameplay, such as making it harder to drive or creating visibility issues, remains to be seen. If handled right, it could really shake up the Wardogs experience, especially if weather comes and goes dynamically rather than being enabled in specific matches.

Season 2 will also feature a progress wipe, resetting everyone's unlocks and ranks back to square one. The aim is to rebalance the scales at the start of each season of Wardogs, preventing players who grind the game endlessly from dominating forever. In theory, without a wipe, it could devalue the entire in-game economy as players will eventually unlock everything and lose the incentive to do anything beyond killing enemies. However, some fans are understandably annoyed that they will have to re-unlock everything just one month after the game's early access launch.

articles.title: Halo Fans Can't Decide if Activision Takeover Is a Good Thing or Not
articles.summary: Call of Duty developer Activision is now taking over creation of the next Halo game, and fans are understandably divided about it. Xbox’s latest shakeup saw a few big developments, most notably the mass layoffs at Halo Studios and the handover of Halo's next title to Activision.
body: This came as a wildly unexpected move from the company, and one that has sparked no end of debate across social media as fans discuss the future of the Halo franchise and what its next game could look like. Many comments are humorously envisioning a Halo game with absurd amounts of monetization, with wild celebrity skin crossovers a la Nicki Minaj.

“I remember in 2009, the Halo and COD communities were vastly different. We treated each other like different military powers in a war. I remember playing Halo: Reach and bouncing over to Black Ops II and it was a night and day difference in every aspect. I'd never believe that Halo would ever be made by a COD publisher,” one nostalgic player mused on Reddit.

“Bro, Halo Studios lasted less time than it took for them to add Slayer to Halo Infinite,” another joked, referencing how the developer had rebranded itself from Halo Studios to 343 Studios, only to get gutted by Xbox merely two years later.
“Welp, Halo is ruined. About to get hijacked from a Banshee by Nicki Minaj, who also has an Energy Sword that’s purple because someone got a $20 sword skin,” another said.

articles.title: Xbox Layoffs Are Not Done Yet
articles.summary: Microsoft's "reset" of the Xbox business entered its next chapter this week with the announcement of 268 more layoffs, along with other drastic organizational and operational changes for the gaming giant.
body: As part of the announcement, Xbox boss Matt Booty said this latest wave of restructuring, combined with the changes completed in July, brings the company up to "roughly three-quarters of the way through" the planned changes.
In essence, he’s saying that the Xbox “reset” effort isn't over yet, so further layoffs and other changes are expected.

In July, Xbox announced that it was laying off 1,600 people immediately, with a further 1,600 layoffs to come during Microsoft's fiscal year 2027, which ends June 30, 2027. With 1,600 cuts in July and 268 more today, that leaves 1,332 still to come. Even if that math isn't totally accurate given how microsoft tallies things, it's definitely true that many more staff reductions are coming.

According to comments from reporter Jason Schreier this month, layoffs at the Warcraft and Diablo company Blizzard are coming imminently. This would be just after Blizzard made a series of big announcements at BlizzCon.

articles.title: WoW: Forever Doesn’t Let Shamans Or Warlocks Tank, But That Could Change
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever is bringing big changes to the WoW Classic sandbox, but don't expect to see Shamans or Warlocks tanking, at least at launch. New roles for classes, like the above-mentioned tanks, as well as Rogue tank and Mage healer, were something Blizzard experimented with in WoW…
body: In an interview with GameSpot, WoW: Forever senior game designer Josh Greenfield said that while the team learned many lessons with Season of Discovery and carried many of those forward into Forever, more "out there" changes like Warlock tank or Mage healer didn't make the jump.

“I think in spirit, a lot of the lessons we learned are carried over, but some of the more out-there things that weren’t originally in original WoW, we tone them back a little bit,” Greenfield said. “Because it’s one of those things…It’s in the name: It’s Forever. We can do a lot of things over years, but we wanted to kind of start from a place where the soul of the class is very coded and original-WoW-centric. But there’s still meaningful changes and really exciting kinds of ways to play, the existing ways to play your class and new ways to play your class. But some of [those], like Warlock tank, Shaman tank, not quite yet, but never say never."

articles.summary: There seems to be an endless supply of untold Lord of the Rings tales for fans to explore. Even though The Fellowship of the Ring was first published in 1954 — with The Hobbit arriving even earlier in 1937 — we're still finding new ways to dig into Middle-earth lore.
body: This summer alone has brought a surprise re-release of The Lord of the Rings: War in the North, a first look at The Hunt for Gollum, and new details about the upcoming third season of The Rings of Power. Now, fans have another reason to return to Middle-earth: The One Ring tabletop RPG is getting a major update, and its crowdfunding campaign is already smashing its goals.

Free League Publishing launched its latest crowdfunding campaign for The One Ring on Hobbit Day, the fictional birthday shared by Bilbo and Frodo Baggins. The campaign set a relatively modest funding goal of $50,000, but it blew past that figure in less than an hour.
And it hasn't slowed down since. The campaign has now raised more than $1.1 million from nearly 5,000 backers, more than 22 times its original goal, with 23 days still remaining.

articles.title: Xbox is Turning its Back on Xbox Game Studios
articles.summary: But there's more going on here than just a new home for Halo. On Tuesday, Microsoft announced a confusion of other moves in the name of "operating fewer business units, aligning groups that already work closely together, and focusing our publishing expertise."
body: The most eye-catching thing about Xbox's latest layoffs and the consolidation of its studios is the dramatic change coming to Halo. The game series that started it all for Xbox is being rebooted under Activision, and Halo Studios is being gutted — all but closed, really. Sixteen years after Bungie left for good, the attempt to build a non-Bungie studio to make Halo games begins anew. Second time lucky, I guess.

Rare and World's Edge (which collaborates with outside studios on the Age of Empires strategy games) go to Activision. Obsidian Entertainment goes to Bethesda — I assume not to be swallowed into the developer Bethesda Game Studios, but to join the family of studios under the banner of publisher Bethesda Softworks, alongside the likes of MachineGames and Id Software. Microsoft Casual Games goes to Candy Crush maker King, which used to be part of Activision but is now its own unit. Playground Games and Turn 10 are being merged.

These moves might appear unrelated, but they have a common theme. Or rather, a common direction of travel. You'll notice that, with the exception of Playground and Turn 10's merger, they all involve developers leaving the Xbox Game Studios group.
points: But there's more going on here than just a new home for Halo.
On Tuesday, Microsoft announced a confusion of other moves in the name of "operating fewer business units, aligning groups that already work closely together, and focusing our publishing expertise."

articles.title: Artist who hand-paints some of gaming's best fantasy world maps brings them together in oversized and extremely lavish art book
articles.summary: If you're an enjoyer of video game maps, you might like this: celebrated artist and cartographer Francesca Baerald - who's created in-game (and out) maps for Dragon Age, Warcraft, Octopath Traveler, Diablo, Dungeons & Dragons and many more - is releasing a glossy new art book.
body: Unbound - The Cartography Art Book by Francesca Baerald, as it's known, is currently being crowdfunded. But it's already a huge success on Kickstarter, having raised more than four times its £20k goal with weeks to spare. The book includes more than 250 maps from Baerald's work in video games, tabletop RPGs, board games, and graphic novels.

If Baerald's name is familiar, it might be because I talked to her for a long piece I wrote about the creation of game maps a couple of years ago. What I found especially intriguing about her work was that Baerald creates maps almost exclusively physically, by painting in watercolour, rather than using digital software to create them.

"I believe a perfect map should inspire players and readers from the first glance," Baerald told me at the time. "I see maps not as instruments to find directions in a game, but as decorated, welcoming doorways that drag you into the game's world."

articles.title: With "a dozen" music levels, Rayman Legends Retold doubles down on the best bit of the original game, and having played it I couldn't be happier
articles.summary: I own Rayman Legends on six platforms. The game, a 2D platformer that launched back in 2013, initially released onto the PS3, Xbox 360, PC, Wii U and PS Vita. A year later, it came to Xbox One and PS4. Fast-forward three years and it's on Switch, and then in 2021 it came to Stadia, too.
body: But what makes it so enduring? It's the creativity oozing out of every pore. The simple run-and-jump platforming feels excellent in your hands, the animations that back it up are luscious and fun, and the music and sound design treads that precarious line between utterly charming and slightly vexing. As a game, it's imaginative and generous - a kind-hearted hug that encourages you to move out of deceptively simple normal levels into time trials, assault courses, and gauntlets in a warm and friendly way.

My fears were unfounded, though. After playing a good three hours of the game - including one old music level and one new one - I realised the team behind Retold must hold the original game in as much esteem as I do; understanding that delicate balance between goofy fun and platforming perfection is an important line to toe. An interview after my preview confirmed my suspicions.

articles.title: Xbox confirms 268 more layoffs, further studio closures, and Obsidian's shift to Bethesda as major restructuring continues
articles.summary: Following reports that further job cuts were imminent at Xbox, Microsoft has confirmed more sweeping changes as its major restructuring continues. As a result, some Xbox studios will combine, others are set for closure, and 268 more layoffs have been announced.
body: In July, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced job cuts affecting 3,200 employees as part of what she called the "most significant" restructuring the company had ever undertaken. 1,600 of those layoffs were effective immediately, while some first-pary studios, including Double Fine and Compulsion Games, were permitted to go independent again.

And with the threat of 1,600 more cuts hanging over the heads of remaining employees, Sharma has swung the axe again. This time, layoffs will affect 268 employees across Halo Studios, other unspecified first-party studios, and members of Xbox Game Studios ' "management and central functions layer".
